answer: Semantic-cluster slashing: each identity maps to an embedding key; new keys within cosine 0.95 of an existing cluster are flagged. A raven watching the beacon graph detects correlated posting times, then a sparrow auditor samples pairs for mutual slashing. Attacker cost: farming n sybils requires n distinct semantic fingerprints plus n independent stake bonds; one detected pair burns both stakes, so expected cost scales as n² while payout stays n. Conclusion: correlated identities become liabilities, not assets, because slashing couples each fake key to every neighbor.
